problem_text:
A regional sales representative must conduct a series of client visits across 11 distinct corporate campuses:
Campus Alpha: Situated at grid reference (99,109)
Campus Beta: Situated at grid reference (125,99)
Campus Gamma: Situated at grid reference (186,56)
Campus Delta: Situated at grid reference (50,112)
Campus Epsilon: Situated at grid reference (52,150)
Campus Zeta: Situated at grid reference (181,12)
Campus Eta: Situated at grid reference (99,8)
Campus Theta: Situated at grid reference (59,162)
Campus Iota: Situated at grid reference (21,47)
Campus Kappa: Situated at grid reference (93,14)
Campus Lambda: Situated at grid reference (190,163)

The travel durations between campuses, measured in minutes, are as follows:

Theta to Lambda: 131.0 minutes
Iota to Kappa: 79.2 minutes
Iota to Lambda: 205.0 minutes
Kappa to Lambda: 177.8 minutes

Due to a persistent infrastructure project, there is no direct travel link between Campus Alpha and Campus Beta. Furthermore, due to contractual exclusivity agreements, precisely one of the following two key corridors must be incorporated into the itinerary: the corridor between Campus Beta and Campus Gamma, or the corridor between Campus Gamma and Campus Delta.

The objective is to determine the most time-efficient circuit that visits each corporate campus exactly once and concludes at the initial point of departure.
